mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 3-month moving average (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (GDPC1) create a dual pressure that elevates recession risk, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while GDPC1 decreases by >3% in the same month
regime_hint: early labor market softening with weak demand
failure_condition: In a 200-day window, the interaction term between PAYEMS and GDPC1 shows no predictive power for 20-day SPX returns (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 3% in a month signals pent-up demand that is released in the following 5-day period, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >3% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 10 such monthly spikes, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of 2% over two months suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which suppresses equity valuations and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for two consecutive months by >2%
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between 2-month INDPRO decline and 20-day SPX returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% in a quarter, it indicates accelerating inflation that the market anticipates, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-on-month change > +2% for any month in the quarter
failure_condition: In 10 such inflationary months, 20-day SPX returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 20-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in unemployment rate (UNRATE) to above 4.5% triggers a risk-off cascade that drives S&P 500 forward returns negative within the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Over 8 such spikes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business (RSAFS) demand series above their 5th percentile moving averages for two consecutive months predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 5th percentile MA and RSAFS > 5th percentile MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 50 such dual-month periods, the interaction term's R-squared for 60-day returns is below 0.05 (no predictive power).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged stagnation in industrial production (INDPRO) for three months indicates structural supply constraints that persistently depress equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns regardless of macro regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains flat for three consecutive months (change < 0.5%)
failure_condition: Across 15 such three-month plateaus, 20-day SPX forward returns show no consistent negative trend (p > 0.1 in linear regression).
